To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) code diversity is a promising technique that can improve the performance of a space-time coded system beyond the performance that could be achieved by using any individual code in that system, (2) code diversity performance gains are largely preserved when the fading prediction is employed, and (3) code diversity can be used in conjunction with low complexity sub-optimal decoding or ML decoding to achieve significant gains.

1) code diversity can be implemented in a practical manner in space-time coded wireless systems, 2) long-range prediction of the time-varying fading channel can be used to compensate for the feedback delay and maintain the performance gains of the instantaneous CSI feedback, 3) oversampled pilot reduction can be used to improve the prediction performance at realistic SNR levels, and 4) a robust low pilot reduction method that employs interleaving can be used to maintain the performance gains at low pilot
